clue.text: Torture instrument suggested by Margaret Hilda Roberts!

definitions.text: Torture instrument suggested by Margaret Hilda Roberts!

parts.words: Torture instrument suggested by Margaret Hilda Roberts!
parts.note: Margaret Hilda Roberts was Margaret Thatcher's name before marriage; she was nicknamed the Iron Lady, so her nickname plus her unmarried status suggest a spiked medieval torture cabinet

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a former prime minister's own name evokes a device of torture.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister 1979-90, was born Margaret Hilda Roberts: a maiden name for the woman the Soviets dubbed the Iron Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a hinged upright coffin lined with spikes, a legendary device for torturing prisoners.

clue.text: Island doctor and I live only to drink

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone stranded on an island with a doctor lives only to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to take liquid in, the formal word for drinking.

clue.text: Obliged to tell the truth by order to Noah

indicators.note: putting things in a new order signals that the letters of to Noah are rearranged

explanation.surface: Noah is commanded to be honest, as if under divine instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn witness has taken a vow and is legally bound to speak truthfully.

clue.text: One who suffers complaints in exemplary fashion

definitions.text: One who suffers complaints in exemplary fashion

parts.words: One who suffers complaints in exemplary fashion
parts.note: complaints here are illnesses, not grumbles: someone ill who bears it perfectly, an ideal person under a doctor's care

explanation.surface: A saintly person who puts up with others' grumbling without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooperative, uncomplaining invalid is the ideal person for nurses and doctors to treat.

clue.text: Cowes yachtsman go from it to a state in America

parts.note: Cowes is the sailing town on the Isle of Wight, abbreviated IOW, from which its yachtsmen set out

explanation.surface: Sailors set off from Cowes heading across the Atlantic to a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes, on the Isle of Wight off England's south coast, is famous for its yachting regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Ribaldry results from unusual heartiness

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of heartiness are put in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Excessive bonhomie tips over into bawdy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthiness is a coarse, frank, down-to-earth quality, much like bawdy humour.

clue.text: Does one find them in play?

definitions.meaning: performs or carries out, as a verb
a stage play is divided into major sections

explanation.surface: A question about whether something turns up during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To do is to perform or behave, and a drama is divided into major sections of that name.

clue.text: French cathedral about to be featured in maps

indicators.note: featured in means placed within, so the short word for about goes inside the word for maps

parts.note: charts are maps, especially for navigators
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A French cathedral turns up on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres, south-west of Paris, has a celebrated Gothic cathedral.

clue.text: Study courses for country people

definitions.meaning: the disciplines taught at school or university
those owing allegiance to a monarch or state, its citizens

explanation.surface: Educational courses designed for rural folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic disciplines are topics of study, and a crown's citizens are its loyal nationals.

clue.text: Norfolk term for a weapon of war

parts.note: the Broads are the lakes and waterways of Norfolk, an English county
a term is a word

explanation.surface: Asking for the Norfolk dialect word for a battle weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England, popular for boating.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, wide-bladed cutting sword, a classic battlefield blade.

clue.text: Talk incessantly about right style of dress

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for chatter surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: to gab is to chatter on and on

explanation.surface: Someone chattering endlessly about the correct way to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, particularly a distinctive outfit or costume.

clue.text: The state of the body politic may depend on it

definitions.text: The state of the body politic may depend on it

parts.words: The state of the body politic may depend on it
parts.note: read one way, a nation's founding law; read another, a person's physical health and makeup

explanation.surface: A remark on what keeps a nation's political system healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a nation's fundamental laws and a person's physical health and build.

clue.text: Courage shown by sober man splitting tree trunk

indicators.note: splitting means breaking into, so the abstainer's letters go inside the word for trunk

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
TT, teetotal, describes someone who never drinks

explanation.surface: A teetotaller shows bravery by chopping a tree trunk in two.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, having nerve or guts is called this.

clue.text: What a driver pulls out to take one's breath away

definitions.meaning: a car's accelerator control, once a knob pulled out from the dashboard

explanation.surface: Something a motorist pulls out that leaves you gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: The engine's fuel control on a vehicle, and also choking someone by the neck.

clue.text: An assortment of men tainted by incarceration

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so the letters of men tainted are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mixed group of corrupt men end up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in custody or imprisoned against one's will.

clue.text: Formulate aims suitable to balance one's budget

parts.note: to formulate is to make or devise
ends are goals or aims
meet is an old word for fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Drawing up appropriate goals in order to keep finances in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having just enough income to cover expenses.

clue.text: Plausible but risky investment ends with debts

indicators.note: ends with means the second piece comes last, after the first

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a risky venture
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A convincing-looking gamble that ultimately leaves you owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemingly reasonable on the surface but actually false, deceptively convincing.

clue.text: Mockery made of holder without an undergarment

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the holder goes around the undergarment

parts.note: a tray holds things for carrying
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Ridicule poured on someone who goes without underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old meaning 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque parody or distorted imitation of something.

clue.text: Guerrillas cheer commitment to the cause

parts.note: partisans are irregular resistance fighters
hip as in hip hip hooray, a cheer

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters rousing support for their cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong, often biased, loyalty to a party or faction.

clue.text: Passionate footballers require return game

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the abbreviation for the footballers is read backwards

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body
a game leg is a lame one

explanation.surface: Keen footballers demand a rematch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return game' reads as a rematch, but 'return' turns the footballers' letters and 'game' means injured, as in a game leg.
explanation.definitionFit: On fire, figuratively: burning with intense feeling.

clue.text: Most eager to put pictures around the study

indicators.note: around means the word for pictures surrounds the word for study

parts.note: pictures are works of art
a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: Someone keen to hang paintings all round their study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' is the intensive sense, as in 'most kind': very eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensely enthusiastic and fervent, burning with zeal.

clue.text: Is unable to install cooker, despite contract

indicators.note: installing puts something inside, so the cooker goes within the word for is unable

parts.note: cant is can't, cannot
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: Someone can't fit a stove, contract or no contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal binding agreement or pledge.

clue.text: Cushion for a foolish old fellow

definitions.meaning: something that softens a blow, as a verb or noun
British slang for a silly old man, as in old duffer

explanation.surface: A soft seat meant for a doddery old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock absorber, and British slang for a dotty elderly man.

clue.text: Typical measure by self-righteous accountant

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A standard measurement taken by a sanctimonious bookkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Typical' puns on typographical: printers measure type in units of this size.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of type size in printing, one-sixth of an inch.

clue.text: Kentish house where gas-burner is not used in roasting

indicators.note: not used means left out, so the letters of the burner are removed from roasting

parts.note: the word the burner is taken from; that the remaining letters also sit together inside it is a coincidence of the deletion
a ring is a burner on a gas hob

explanation.surface: A Kent building where roasting happens without a gas burner.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring's letters come out scattered: R from the front, ING from the end. Kent, in south-east England, is hop country.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln building for drying hops, characteristic of the Kent countryside.

clue.text: To walk in front of one friend is quite right

indicators.note: in front of places the walking piece before the rest

parts.note: leg it is slang for walk or run
I is the Roman numeral for one
mate is British for friend

explanation.surface: Walking ahead of a pal is perfectly proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful, valid, entirely proper.

clue.text: A Hebridean isle sounds like heaven

indicators.note: sounds like means a word said aloud matches the answer

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: An island off Scotland whose name evokes paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Rearranging mat in a tent is an accomplishment

indicators.note: rearranging means the letters of mat in a tent are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Tidying a camping mat inside the tent counts as an achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: Achievement, something gained through effort.
